plain.li: [first] A year here today. I remember the first night in the {PLACE} better than most of what came after.
[years] {YEARS} years since the founding. We ate well and told the old stories again.
Founding day. Someone counted the graves and someone else counted the buildings, and we drank to both.
[tradition] Founding day, done the way we always do it. I like knowing what comes next, for once.
[winter] Founding day in the snow. I thought about the first winter and put another log on.

warm.li: Founding day. I looked round the table and thought: we made this, all of us.

blunt.li: Founding day. Good food. Same stories.

cheerful.li: Founding day! I ate until I had to lie down on the bench.

gloomy.li: Another founding day. Fewer of the first faces at the table every year.

cold.li: Founding day. A useful ritual. People work harder for a place they've celebrated.

plain.li: [new] Brought the first real harvest in today. My back hurts and the bins are full.
[new] We've got a harvest in, the first one that was all ours: sown, grown and cut.
[!new,first] A year since the first harvest. Hard to believe how worried we were about that one field.
[!new,years] Harvest day again, {YEARS} years on. Fresh bread at supper, and nobody had to ration it.
[!new] Harvest day. Ate well. The fields will want me again tomorrow.
[!new,tradition] Harvest day, kept the old way. I hung a sheaf over my door like everyone else.

warm.li: [!new] Harvest day. Thanked the ones who worked the fields with me, and meant every word.
[new] All those weeks of weeding, and today it paid off. I could have hugged every one of them.

blunt.li: [!new] Harvest day. Good. Back to the fields tomorrow.

cheerful.li: [!new] Harvest day! I had thirds and nobody stopped me.
[new] Our first harvest! I danced in the field and I'm not sorry.

gloomy.li: [!new] Harvest day. One good year doesn't promise the next.
[new] A harvest at last. Now we find out whether it lasts the winter.

cold.li: [!new] Harvest day. The stores are adequate, which is worth marking.
[new] First harvest in. Yield acceptable. Morale noticeably better.

plain.li: [new] Snow, the first we've had here. The whole place looks different under it.
[new] First snow here. Fetched extra wood before supper, in case.
[!new] First snow of the winter. We took the afternoon for games, and I came back soaked to the knees.
[!new] The first snow came, and with it the snowball fight. I lost.
[!new,years] {YEARS} winters of first snows here now. It still makes the morning feel new.
[!new,child] I made the biggest snowball anyone has ever seen. Then it broke.

warm.li: [!new] Watched the first snow with a hot cup and good company. I didn't want the afternoon to end.

blunt.li: [!new] First snow. Cold feet. The games were fine.

cheerful.li: [!new] First snow day! I won the sled race, or at least nobody can prove I didn't.

gloomy.li: [!new] First snow. Pretty for a day, then months of cold.

cold.li: [!new] First snow. The games kept spirits up ahead of a hard season. Worth the lost afternoon.
[new] First snowfall. The firewood stock will need checking.

plain.li: [clean,first] A year since we beat {ENEMY}. I walked the line where we held them.
[clean,years] {YEARS} years since {ENEMY} came. We feasted, and someone told it as if we were never scared.
[clean] The day we beat {ENEMY}. I still hear it sometimes when I'm falling asleep.
[fallen] The day we fought {ENEMY} and lost {DEAD}. I went out to the graves after supper.
[fallen,first] A year since {DEAD} fell. I keep going over what I could have done differently.
[fallen,years] {YEARS} years since the battle with {ENEMY}. It doesn't get any further away, only quieter.
[nemesis] The day {ENEMY} fell. I remember sleeping right through that night.

warm.li: [fallen] Told the young ones about {DEAD} today, and how brave {DEAD} was. They should know.
[clean] Thought about everyone who stood with me that day. I'd do it again, with them.

blunt.li: [clean] Anniversary of the fight with {ENEMY}. We won. That's what matters.
[fallen] {DEAD} should still be here. That's all I've got to say about today.

cheerful.li: [clean] Victory day! The story gets better every time we tell it.

gloomy.li: [fallen] The battle day again. I can still smell the smoke when I think about it.
[clean] The day we beat {ENEMY}. They'll be back one day. They always are.

cold.li: [clean] Anniversary of the defense against {ENEMY}. {COUNT} of theirs, none of ours. A good exchange.
[fallen] The day we lost {DEAD} to {ENEMY}. I have thought since about where the line was weak.

plain.li: [first] A year since {DEAD} died. I kept expecting to hear {DEAD} at supper.
[years] {YEARS} years without {DEAD}. Some days I can't remember the voice. Today I could.
Went to {DEAD}'s grave today and told {DEAD} what's happened since. It took a while.
We kept the day for {DEAD}. Someone told the story about the burnt stew and the whole table laughed.
[kin] It's the day {DEAD} died. I didn't get much work done. Nobody asked me to.
[kin,years] {YEARS} years. I still keep some of {DEAD}'s things in a box under my bed.

warm.li: Remembered {DEAD} today, all the good of {DEAD}. There was a lot of it.
[kin] Talked to {DEAD} at the grave the way we used to talk at the table. I think {DEAD} would have liked the news.

blunt.li: {DEAD}'s day. Went to the grave. Came back. Worked.
[kin] I miss {DEAD}. I don't need a day for that, but we had one.

cheerful.li: We remembered {DEAD} today with stories instead of tears, mostly.

gloomy.li: Remembered {DEAD} today. Remembering doesn't bring anyone back.
[kin] The day {DEAD} died. I stayed at the grave until it got dark.

cold.li: The day {DEAD} died. I observed it. The others seemed to need me to.

plain.li: [first] A year married to {OTHER_nameDef}. It feels shorter and longer at once.
[years] {YEARS} years with {OTHER_nameDef}. We sat up late and talked about the wedding.
Our wedding day. {OTHER_nameDef} made me laugh at the feast, the same way as the first time.
Wedding day. The others made more of it than we did, and I didn't mind.
[tradition] Our wedding day, and the colony threw us a feast again. I've given up telling them not to.

warm.li: A year more with {OTHER_nameDef}. I'm lucky, and I said so.
Our wedding day. I held {OTHER_nameDef}'s hand all through supper.

blunt.li: Wedding day. {OTHER_nameDef} remembered. I nearly didn't.

cheerful.li: Our wedding day! {OTHER_nameDef} still dances terribly. I love it.

gloomy.li: Our wedding day. I worry about how many more we'll get, out here.

cold.li: The anniversary of my marriage to {OTHER_nameDef}. The arrangement continues to suit me.

plain.li: [first] A year since {OTHER_nameDef} turned up. I can't picture the place without {OTHER_objective} now.
[years] {YEARS} years since {OTHER_nameDef} came. I remember the first thing {OTHER_nameDef} said to me, and I won't write it down.
{OTHER_nameDef} came here on this day, back when we had almost nothing. I'm glad {OTHER_pronoun} stayed.

warm.li: Told {OTHER_nameDef} today that I'm glad {OTHER_pronoun} came. {OTHER_nameDef} pretended not to be pleased.

blunt.li: [years] {OTHER_nameDef}'s been here {YEARS} years. Still owes me for that first meal.

cheerful.li: It's the day {OTHER_nameDef} arrived! I made {OTHER_objective} sit at the head of the table.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} came here the same week we nearly starved. Strange, what sticks.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} joined on this day. A good addition, on the whole.

plain.li: [self] My birthday. Someone remembered, and then everyone did.
[self] Another year older. They saved me the best seat at supper.
[self,old] My birthday. I asked them not to count, and they counted anyway.
[self,child] It's my birthday! I'm older now. I checked.
[friend] It's {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. I gave {OTHER_objective} something I made.
[friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday today. We sang, badly.
[friend,lowtech] Carved a little figure for {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. It's meant to be a muffalo.

warm.li: [self] My birthday, and everyone was so kind I didn't know where to look.
[friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. I told {OTHER_objective} what a difference {OTHER_pronoun} makes here.

cheerful.li: [self] My birthday! Cake, or the nearest thing we could manage.
[friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday! I hid behind the door and jumped out, and {OTHER_nameDef} nearly hit me.

gloomy.li: [self] Another birthday out here. I didn't expect to see this one.
[friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. I hope we all see the next one.

cold.li: [self] My birthday. The attention was unnecessary, though not unwelcome.
[friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. I made the expected gesture.

plain.li: [first,named] The first {NAME}. We didn't know how it's done yet, so we ate.
{NAME} today. A feast, and nobody had to stand watch through supper.
[years] {NAME} again. Same songs as last year, and I still don't know the words.
{NAME}. I ate too much and talked too long, and I'd do both again.
[tradition] {NAME}, kept like every year. It's starting to feel like ours.

warm.li: {NAME}. Sat with people I don't usually talk to. Glad I did.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. Feasting while the stores go down. Someone has to worry about it.

cold.li: {NAME}. A feast is an efficient way to keep people content.

plain.li: {NAME} today. We named the dead one by one at supper. It took longer than last year.
[first,named] The first {NAME}. I didn't know what to say at the graves, so I stood there with the others.
{NAME}. Work went slowly and nobody minded.
[tradition] {NAME}. Every year we stop for this, and every year I'm glad we do.

warm.li: {NAME}. Thought about everyone we've lost and what each of them gave this place.

blunt.li: {NAME}. Visited the graves. Back to work tomorrow.

cheerful.li: {NAME}. We told funny stories about the dead. They'd have wanted that.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. The list of names gets longer every year.

cold.li: {NAME}. A day to remember the dead. I remembered them.

plain.li: {NAME}. Didn't lift a hand all afternoon. Strange feeling.
[first,named] Our first {NAME}. I didn't know what to do with myself until about noon, and then I did nothing very well.
[years] {NAME} again. I slept until the sun was high and nobody shouted.
[!winter] {NAME}. Spent the afternoon lying in the grass.
[winter] {NAME}. Stayed by the fire all afternoon with my boots off.
[tradition] {NAME}, the one day a year the colony stops. Everyone needs it.
[trait:Industrious] {NAME}. Everyone else rested. I fixed the gate.

warm.li: {NAME}. Spent the afternoon talking with friends, with nothing to rush off to.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I took two naps and I'm calling it an accomplishment.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. Rested, which only gave me time to think.

cold.li: {NAME}. Lost work today, offset by rested workers tomorrow.

plain.li: {NAME}. Ran in the footrace and came in near the back, where I usually am.
[first,named] The first {NAME}. We made up most of the rules as we went.
[years] {NAME} again. Same games, same arguments over the rules.
{NAME}. I won the throwing contest. Nobody believes me, so I'm writing it down.
[winter] {NAME} in the snow. The snowball fight went on until it was too dark to aim.
[tradition] {NAME}. Last year's champion lost, and we may never hear the end of it.

warm.li: {NAME}. Cheered for everyone, even the ones who beat me.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I won something, though nobody agrees on what.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. Pulled something in the races. Worth it, maybe.

cold.li: {NAME}. I won by watching the others. The games are mostly about that.
